Hydra design system · Discovery · 19 Oct 2026

Reusable content molecules across ConnectED modules

A visual audit of BOM, Release Notes, Part Search, SPEC, Admin and Content flows. It looks for cards and self-contained content blocks that repeat in at least two modules and should become one Hydra molecule driven by properties. Discovery only: nothing was changed in Figma.

Product molecules
1

Choice List Row

One compact, selectable row inside a list of options (radio or checkbox), with a label, optional secondary line and a trailing count.

New4 modules · 5 samplesContentPart SearchSPECBOM
Why new

Today every module draws this row as plain frames inside a modal slot, with no shared component. The same 3-part anatomy (control · label · trailing meta) repeats in 3 modules, and the only differences are content, control type and whether a secondary line shows. Hydra's base Radio/Checkbox are atoms and don't carry the row chrome (fill, divider, selected background, trailing meta).

When to use vs. related

Option Card: use when there are only 2–4 rich choices, each with a description or icon, laid out as cards. Use Choice List Row for longer, scannable lists of named things (packages, BOMs, master SPECs), often with search or scrolling above.

Destination

Hydra file → Molecules page

Not observed yet

2

Selection Summary

A tinted, read-only panel at the top of a modal that tells the user what they are acting on (“Adding…”, “These parts will be added”, “Selected file”).

New3 modules · 6 samplesContentPart SearchBOM
Why new

This context block appears in every “add to / move to” modal across 3 modules, always built from frames. It is purely presentational: an eyebrow label plus 1–N value lines in a soft panel. That's simple enough to be a clean new molecule, and no existing Hydra molecule needs to stretch to cover it.

When to use vs. related

Attribute List shows label/value pairs about one object. Selection Summary shows which objects are about to be affected, as a single list under one eyebrow.

Destination

Hydra file → Molecules page

3

Empty State Block

Centred illustration, title, optional explanation and optional next-step button for a list or section with nothing in it yet.

New3 modules · 7 samplesContentBOMAdmin
Why new

Every module wraps the AntD “Empty” illustration instance in its own frame, adding a title, description and CTA by hand, and title size and spacing drift between them. One molecule that wraps the atom with optional description and action slots covers all of them without touching the atom itself.

When to use vs. related

The AntD Empty illustration stays an atom inside this block. Don't use this block for errors or “not found” search results; those use Alert or a result pattern (see Open questions).

Destination

Hydra file → Molecules page

4

Option Card

A bordered card for picking one of a few rich choices (export route, document format, entry action), with optional icon, title, description and radio.

New (promote BOM local component)2 modules · 5 samplesBOMSPEC
Why new

BOM already has local components for this (ExportCard, Export / Format Card, Shared / Export Format Card with Rest/Hover). SPEC rebuilt the same card from frames for its export options. Promoting one clean version to Hydra removes three BOM local copies and the SPEC frames. The radio is an optional element, not a different interaction: all of them are single-choice cards.

When to use vs. related

Choice List Row is for long, compact lists. Option Card is for 2–4 important choices that need a description, an icon, or a large click target. Static info cards (no selection) should not use this molecule.

Destination

Hydra file → Molecules page

File Upload Dropzone

A dashed drop area that walks a single file through empty → uploading → selected → error, inside an upload modal.

New2 modules · 7 samplesSPECAdmin
Why new

Admin (Release Notes bulk upload) and SPEC (Upload a SPEC) built the same 4-state dropzone independently, from frames, with different button emphasis and progress styles. One molecule with a State variant gives both flows identical behaviour. AntD Upload.Dragger is only the empty drop area, not the full state set.

When to use vs. related

BOM's “Upload a file” is an Option Card entry point that opens an upload flow. It's a different job. The Selection Summary (success tone) can show the chosen file after the dropzone step.

Open questions before implementation

  • Check Hydra's Molecules page before building.

    Per your answer I didn't audit Hydra's existing molecules, and the connector only lists the Hydra file's “Cover” and “Logo” pages. Please confirm none of these 8 already exist there. If one does, its decision flips from New to Upgrade.

  • Option Card: one component for “entry action” and “pick a route”?

    BOM uses the same local card both for navigating (Get started) and for choosing (Export route). I recommend one molecule with Control = None | Radio. Say if you'd rather split them.

  • File Upload Dropzone: pick one button emphasis and one progress style.

    Admin uses a primary button and a progress bar. SPEC uses a secondary button and a spinner. I'd default to secondary and a bar.

  • Stat Tile: keep both Row and Stacked layouts?

    Only 2 modules, 3 samples. Keeping both is cheap. Dropping Stacked means restyling the Admin import result.

  • Result panel: watchlist, not proposed yet.

    Admin “Import complete”, SPEC “Document ready” and CFM “Publish success/failure” all report an outcome, but their structures differ (centred result vs inline alert). Worth revisiting once the CFM publish screens are inspected in detail.

  • Flow Doc Card: where should it live?

    In Hydra → Molecules (with a “Docs” prefix), or in a separate design-ops utility file?

  • Part Search detail hero.

    Excluded as a page header. If you want a Large size of Part Summary Card for it, that's an easy extra variant later.

Coverage

Tool: official Figma MCP connector, read-only (get_metadata for structure, get_screenshot for the visual check). Method: a full structural sweep of every linked node, then a visual pass on representative screens per section, using common sense rather than a per-layer inspection (as agreed). Archived work: none found inside the linked nodes. Hydra's existing molecules were not audited (per your answer). No access problems.
